clue.text: Part of my itinerary, goosey gander

definitions.text: Part of my itinerary, goosey gander

parts.words: Part of my itinerary, goosey gander
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'Goosey goosey gander, whither shall I wander? Upstairs and ...' lists the gander's route, and the clue asks for the second stop on it

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Goosey goosey gander, whither shall I wander? Upstairs and downstairs and in my lady's chamber'; the answer is one leg of that trip.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the gander wanders to the lower floor of the house, one stage of its wandering route.

clue.text: Old price of the bilingual puss

parts.note: du is French for 'of the', so the bilingual speaker says it in French
puss is a cat

explanation.surface: An old price paid for a cat that speaks two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual' tells you to switch 'of the' into French, DU. A ducat was an old European gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold coin once used across Europe served as an old unit of money in which prices were paid.

clue.text: Glutton in guise of a toothy granny ?

definitions.meaning: glutton is another name for this voracious animal of the weasel family

definitions.text: in guise of a toothy granny ?
definitions.meaning: the wolf in Little Red Riding Hood dresses as the grandmother and shows big teeth, so a wolf-like beast fits

explanation.surface: A greedy eater disguised as a grandmother with big teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glutton' looks like a greedy person; it is the animal's other name. The second part recalls the wolf in grandmother's clothes in Little Red Riding Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The stocky carnivore of the weasel family is known as the glutton for its appetite, and its name suggests a wolf.

clue.text: It's a turning-point for June

parts.note: June sounds like a woman's name having a crisis, but means the month in which the sun turns back on its course

explanation.walkthrough: 'June' could be a person; it is the month, around 21 June, when days stop lengthening in the northern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest day, in late June, is when the sun reaches its northern limit and turns back.

clue.text: Sailors oye a copper and vamoose

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so ABS are sailors
to con is to study or scan with the eye
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Seamen eye up a policeman and run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a copper' looks like a policeman, but means a penny, D in old British money (pounds, shillings and pence).
explanation.definitionFit: To vamoose is slang for to leave hurriedly, the same as running off secretly.

clue.text: Dire effects can be as grave

indicators.note: can be signals what the letters of the following words can be made into

explanation.surface: Terrible consequences may be as serious as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges the letters of AS GRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Destruction and devastating damage are the dire effects of war or disease.

clue.text: Salvo misfires: nothing goes off for Serge

indicators.note: a salvo that misfires goes wrong, so the remaining letters are rearranged
something that goes off leaves, so this letter departs from the word salvo

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A volley of gunfire fails, with nothing going off at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' takes O from SALVO, leaving SALV, and 'misfires' rearranges those letters. 'Serge' looks like the fabric, but here it is a man's first name, typically Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a typically Russian given name, and a Russian is an example of an East European of that ethnic family.

clue.text: Look at the hot state of French currency

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
ire is anger, a heated state of mind

explanation.surface: Examining the overheated condition of the French franc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money (the franc), but means a current: the longest river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current of water, and this is France's longest one, flowing to the Atlantic at Nantes.

clue.text: In his deliberations he might observe the garments of the cloth

definitions.text: In his deliberations he might observe the garments of the cloth

parts.words: In his deliberations he might observe the garments of the cloth
parts.note: a parish committee member meets in the room where the clergy's robes are kept, so he sees their vestments

explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' means the clergy; parish business was once conducted in the room where vestments are stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the parish vestry met in the church room holding clerical robes to run parish affairs.

clue.text: Bad hat, or one whose virtue seeks no reward ?

definitions.meaning: an old British slang term for a worthless rascal

definitions.text: one whose virtue seeks no reward
definitions.meaning: a person who is virtuous without payment, read literally as good without return

explanation.surface: A scoundrel, or a saint who never expects thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad hat' is old British slang for a rogue. Read literally, the answer describes someone good for no payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless idler is useless, while a person who does good free of charge is literally virtuous in return for no reward.

clue.text: Something for writing in water

parts.note: reads like an impossible pen, but means a reed pen whose plant grows in water

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe writing on water; in fact the reed that grows in water was cut to make an old pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The calamus was the reed pen of the ancients, cut from a reed that grows in marshes and shallows.

clue.text: Is lovin' when bowed'

indicators.note: bowed means bent out of shape, so the letters of the clue's first two words are twisted round

explanation.surface: Someone is in love once they bow, like a courtly suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' signals the rearrangement of IS LOVIN', and also describes how the instruments are played, so the whole clue serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringed instruments of the orchestra are sounded by drawing a bow across their strings.

clue.text: Particularly suitable for "The Egoist " as a musical

definitions.text: Particularly suitable for "The Egoist " as a musical

parts.words: Particularly suitable for "The Egoist " as a musical
parts.note: an egoist's favourite tune would be all about 'me', and a recurring tune in a musical is its signature number

explanation.walkthrough: The Egoist is a novel by George Meredith; split the answer as THE ME SONG and it suits a self-centred hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical's recurring signature tune is its main melody, identified with the show or a character.

clue.text: Mariana's mood

parts.note: Mariana, in Tennyson's poem, sits in the moated grange repeating that her life is gloomy and that he cometh not

explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's 'Mariana' has the refrain 'My life is dreary, He cometh not'; the answer is the shorter form of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's heroine is forlorn and gloomy, and the poetic adjective for that dismal state is the answer.

clue.text: Doctor could sip drop by drop

indicators.note: could hints at what the word sip could become if its letters were rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician might take small sips of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' asks for what SIP might become, IPS; put after DR. 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that falls a bead at a time is said to trickle in that way, falling in small drops.

clue.text: Pence come to one exact shilling in the provinces

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for pence in old British money
one is the Roman numeral I
strict means exact or precise
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Pennies make up exactly one shilling out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: D and S are pence and shillings in pre-decimal British money (from Latin denarius and solidus).
explanation.definitionFit: Regions or administrative areas of a country are its provinces.

clue.text: It's absolutely undemocratic!

parts.note: absolutely plays on absolute rule, the opposite of democracy

explanation.walkthrough: 'absolutely' reads as an intensifier, but it points to absolute power held by one ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by a tyrant with absolute power is the very opposite of government by the people.

clue.text: Both ways I'm receiving an allowance for settling in

parts.note: the letters of I'm written forwards and then backwards
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: In both directions, I am getting money to help me move house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both ways' gives IM and then MI. The definition names one who is settling in a new country.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer settling in a foreign land to live there permanently.

clue.text: Mettlesome timpanists ?

parts.note: mettlesome sounds like metal-some, describing drummers whose instruments are made of metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mettlesome' means spirited, but it sounds like metal: Caribbean bands play drums made from oil drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribbean groups play tuned pans hammered from oil drums, so their percussionists beat on metal.

clue.text: Dogs' home ?

parts.note: a breed of German shepherd dog takes its name from a region, read as the place those dogs come from

explanation.walkthrough: A dogs' home sounds like an animal shelter; it means the region (Alsace, in Latin) that named the breed of German shepherd dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for the region of Alsace, the supposed home of the breed of German shepherd dog.

clue.text: Lowers sea-beds

parts.note: reads as dredging the ocean floor, but the letters of sea-beds make a verb for degrading

explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram signal: the clue simply offers SEA-BEDS, whose letters rearranged give a word for lowers, as in lowering standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower the value or quality of something is to degrade it.

clue.text: Name of females of the species only ?

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for a name, used for a Roman's family name

definitions.text: of females of the species only ?
definitions.meaning: a group of females only has no males in it, read as two words

explanation.surface: A naturalist names a group of animals that are all female.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO MEN for the second definition; the first is the Latin for name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman's clan name is called by the Latin word for name, and a females-only group contains no males.

clue.text: Fix attention with a hammer ?

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a metal bolt hammered flat

explanation.surface: Concentrate hard, as though nailing something down.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as a fresh reading: fixing done with a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping show holds the gaze fixed; a metal pin hammered over joins plates fast.

clue.text: House that offers Hamlet no come-back for example

indicators.note: no tells us the following letters are missing from the word for hamlet

parts.note: a hamlet is a small village

indicators.note: come-back tells us to turn the abbreviation round, reading it backwards

explanation.surface: A house where Hamlet gets no reply, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the prince, but means a small VILLAGE. 'come-back' turns EG into GE, and 'no' removes it from VILLAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country or suburban house is called by the Latin-derived name for a dwelling.

clue.text: Peasant footwear at times damages the plant

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog worn by French peasants
ages means long times or eras

explanation.surface: Peasants' clogs sometimes wreck the machinery in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' here means a factory, not a growing thing; the word is said to come from workers throwing clogs into machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately wrecking a factory's machinery is the classic deliberate destruction by workers or enemies.

clue.text: Editor in lieu ?

definitions.meaning: W. T. ..., the crusading Victorian editor of the Pall Mall Gazette
in place of, as in the phrase 'in his place'

explanation.definitionFit: W. T. Stead was a famous Victorian newspaper editor, and the word also means place, as in 'in someone's place'.

clue.text: Cotton town: many rupees turn on one piece of it

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn round the word for many rupees, reading it backwards

parts.note: a lac (lakh) is a hundred thousand rupees in India
one is the Roman numeral I
a cut is a piece, as of meat or cloth

explanation.surface: In an Indian cotton town, lots of money is spent on each piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses LAC to CAL; then I and CUT. CALICUT, now Kozhikode in Kerala, gave its name to calico cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian port of Kerala gave its name to calico, the cotton cloth exported from it.

clue.text: Pointed way of changing cap and ties

indicators.note: a way of changing the letters of the two short words is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A sharp way to swap your cap and ties for new ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way of changing' rearranges the letters of CAP and TIES together; the result is a botanical word for spiked.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the word describes a flower head arranged in a spike, so having a pointed form.

clue.text: Dramatic wood

definitions.meaning: the playwright George Bernard ..., author of Pygmalion
a dialect word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright is the dramatist of that surname; the old word for a copse or thicket is spelt the same.

clue.text: As a prophet or his pupils

definitions.meaning: a prophet sees well into the future
pupils are the openings of the eyes, which may see distant objects better than near ones

explanation.surface: A seer and the disciples he teaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like students of the prophet, but means the openings of his eyes: long-sighted eyes see far better than near.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet has foresight about the future; long-sighted eyes see distant things clearly.
